sections.h2: Which Durham offices send my property tax bill?
sections.html:
One county department does the work for the whole city. Durham County Tax Administration lists property, assesses it and collects the money, while the City of Durham decides only its own rate. In person, go to 201 East Main Street, 3rd Floor, Administration Building II, Durham, NC 27701, any weekday from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, or call 919-560-0300.

The county's own page splits the department into six areas: License and Fees, Payment and Collections, Personal Property, Real Property, Tax Help and Tax Relief. Mailed payments go to Durham County Tax Collector, PO Box 3397, Durham, NC 27702-3397, and the county asks residents never to mail cash. In foreclosure suits the plaintiffs are the City and County of Durham, which shows how closely the two governments share collection.

sections.h2: What combined tax rate applies to a home inside Durham city limits?
sections.html:
For fiscal year 2026-27 the county prints $0.4371 for the city and $0.5792 for the county, a combined $1.0163. The City of Durham's own budget news confirms the city piece at 43.71 cents per $100 of assessed value.

City and county rates for three fiscal years, as listed on the county's Tax Rates page

The county reappraised real property effective January 1, 2025, and the second row is the first year printed after that change. A parcel inside the City of Durham Business Improvement District carries a combined rate of $1.0863 for 2026-27. The same page prints a solid waste fee of $185.00 for the 2026-27 year, plus separate lines for Morrisville, Cary, Raleigh and Chapel Hill.

Budget adoption wraps up in mid to late June, and new rates start July 1. The city's adopted 2026-27 budget totals $767 million, holds the property tax rate where it was, and raises water and sewer rates 12% for the average customer. Stormwater and parking rates did not change.

sections.h2: What dates matter for paying Durham property tax?
sections.html:
Tax is billed with a September 1 due date, yet the county gives you until January 5 before interest starts. From January 6, interest runs 2% for month one and three quarters of one percent per month afterward, following G.S. 105-360.

  • If the fifth lands on a Saturday or Sunday, paying the next business day is still on time.
  • Monthly plans cover real property only and must be set up before the bill goes delinquent.
  • Escrow accounts usually send their payment in late November.
  • Cards add a processing fee, while online electronic checks cost nothing.
  • A bounced check brings a $25 penalty, after which only cash or certified funds are taken.

sections.h2: How can a Durham owner challenge a new assessed value?
sections.html:
File with the county before its Board of Equalization and Review stops taking appeals. The 2026 cutoff was June 17 at 5:00 p.m., and it has passed. The county favors the online appeal on its Tax Help page, which lets you message staff and track your case, with a paper form as the fallback.

Durham appraised all real estate as of January 1, 2025. Staff say they can speak only to the appraised value, leaving the size of an increase, affordability and service levels aside. Between reappraisals the county may adjust a parcel only for events such as rezoning or a change to the buildings. A homeowner who loses before the county board has 30 days from the mailing of the decision to notify the state Property Tax Commission, per G.S. 105-290.

sections.h2: What relief programs does Durham County list for homeowners?
sections.html:
The Tax Relief page describes three homestead programs plus help through the county Department of Social Services for low income owners. Applications are due June 1, and the county invites calls at 919-560-0300.

  • An elderly or disabled exclusion with a one time application and a $38,800 income cap.
  • A circuit breaker deferment that holds tax to a percentage of income and needs a fresh application each year.
  • A disabled veteran exclusion of up to $45,000 of appraised value.

The county adds that deferred circuit breaker tax is repaid when the owner dies, sells or moves, with the most recent three years due. That makes a sale the moment to ask the assessor for the deferred balance.

sections.h2: What can Durham County do when a property tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid real property tax is a lien, and the county may hire private attorneys to foreclose under G.S. 105-374 after notices and a pre-foreclosure letter. The owner of record on the delinquency date, January 6, appears in a required newspaper notice, and a payment plan does not prevent that.

  • Bank attachment: the bank freezes accounts for ten days or until the tax office confirms payment.
  • Wage garnishment: the statutory deduction is 10% of gross pay each period.
  • State refund setoff: the state adds a $5.00 fee and a $15.00 administrative fee.
  • Sheriff levy: personal property can be seized and sold, with a $75.00 towing fee when a vehicle is taken.

After assignment to an attorney, the tax office stops accepting direct payments, and the payoff must cover taxes, interest, fees and costs through the attorney. Auctions run monthly on the second Tuesday at 12:00pm in the lobby of the Durham County Judicial Building, 510 Dillard Street. The high bidder deposits 10%, then an upset bid window stays open for 10 days. Redemption by the owner remains possible until the court confirms the sale. Durham County sells no tax liens, since the legislature ended that in 1983.

sections.h2: How does Durham property tax change what I do when I sell?
sections.html:
Whoever owned the parcel on January 1 is billed for that year, and a former owner is told to pass a stray bill to the buyer. Have your closing attorney explain how the year is shared, and get a written balance from the tax collector before choosing a closing date.

If the parcel has already gone to a foreclosure attorney, only that attorney can quote a payoff. Plan the closing date around that quote. Owners with deferred circuit breaker tax should ask the assessor for the figure that comes due on transfer.

sections.h2: How large is Durham and what do homes cost there?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's city profile gives the base that these tax rates apply to.

  • 305,561 residents on the July 2025 estimate, a 7.6% rise over the 2020 base.
  • 112.79 square miles of land, which works out to 2,513.6 residents per square mile at the 2020 count.
  • Owners live in 52.3% of homes, and those homes have a median value of $392,800.
  • Middle household income of $81,619, with gross rent in the middle at $1,508.
  • 126,550 households of about 2.21 people each.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to pay Durham property tax without interest?
faqs.a: January 5. Billing starts with a September 1 due date, and interest begins on January 6. A weekend January 5 pushes the cutoff to Monday, and registered vehicles follow their own schedule.

faqs.q: Does the Durham City Council set the property tax rate?
faqs.a: The council sets the city share through the budget it adopts each June, and the county commissioners set the county share. The two combine on one bill, and new rates take effect July 1.

faqs.q: Can I get a payment plan for my Durham property tax?
faqs.a: Yes for real property bills, if you arrange it before the bill turns delinquent. Until January 5 you can also pay in pieces with no formal agreement.

faqs.q: If I sold my Durham house in March, who owes that year's bill?
faqs.a: The county bills the owner of record on January 1, even after a sale. It advises forwarding the bill to the new owner, so settle the split with your closing attorney.

faqs.q: How do I stop a Durham tax foreclosure?
faqs.a: Contact the attorney assigned to the parcel for a redemption figure and pay taxes, interest, fees and costs before the court confirms the sale. A federal bankruptcy filing can also halt the process.
